# Original cursor SQL expression supplement

This is an independent, static original-only supplement. No original case, candidate, native image, VM, SQLite connection or subprocess has been executed here. The existing read oracle's 86 base cases and 6,286 frozen derived cases are untouched. This directory contains a different finite SQL-expression inventory; its count must not be substituted for that original inventory.

The complete 46-line `_hia_read` is extracted from actual published e7c1729345d5d06757b38a6ae1ce54ae9790fd85. The observer compiles that body without editing any expression. No HIA control graph was used to construct expectations. Expected observations do not yet exist. The executable entry point runs exactly one named original case per fresh process, with product imports, ctypes, SQLite, subprocesses and network effects forbidden.

## Declared fake-provider boundaries

The data-get Store is explicitly owned by the fake Service. SQL Stores can be persistent, temporary, or intentionally cyclic. SQL databases can be separately owned by the Service or owned only by a temporary Store and its bound callable/cursor. Execute and fetchone providers have distinct normal-method, owner-retaining callable, and detached-callable inputs. A detached callable keeps only its receiver's label, its own result payload and the observer. It does not keep the receiver. An SQL cursor's optional database ownership is an explicit input, not an inferred relationship.

Trace records hold only canonical values and labels. Identity labels are accepted only while the recorded weak reference still names that exact object; stale numeric IDs are not accepted. Rebinding actions run at declared original tuple getters, after original method capture. They never replay the Service or database getter. The test observer may dereference its declared weak current-Store link to perform an explicit rebind action; this is an input provider effect, not a proposed production ownership-discovery mechanism.

The cases retain both SQL statements' complete original lookup and argument order, their fake execute boundary and post-effect boundary, SELECT's chained fetchone, INSERT's ignored return, the metadata local, cursor/connection/callable destruction, and the returned artifact reference. Separate cases inject AttributeError at exact lookup points, including its original name/obj metadata. Provider ValueError, StopIteration and KeyboardInterrupt are retained as their original classes and identities. Each input is repeated as two declared contexts: no active handler and an active outer KeyError.

The observer keeps actual results and errors until an explicit consumer-release phase. It never clears traceback fields or normalizes exception metadata to force collection. Caller input release and a declared final garbage-collection phase follow. Additional tuple-time garbage collection is present only in the specifically named cyclic-Store cases. Numeric collection returns and all observed destructor events remain recorded; they are not normalized. Exact traceback frames are preserved in a separate raw file so a future semantic comparison does not mistake transport stack frames for business behavior. Post-snapshot events are kept separately and cannot modify the canonical snapshot.

## Intended execution, pending authorization

Example for one fixed input:

```
python -I -B -S sql_original_oracle.py --case-id sql.select-and-insert.outer0 --output /absolute/new-evidence/case
```

A future supervisor must run every frozen case in fresh, isolated processes, retain complete stdout/stderr and process outcomes, and compare two same-runtime original observations before any candidate executes. This draft deliberately does not create a process supervisor or run itself. Current Python 3.12/3.13/3.14 history differences must be recorded separately; no original callsite is silently warmed or reset inside a production gate.

## What this does not establish

The SQL implementations are fake. Registration, resource generation, child-native delivery, ResourceScope, ACK, outer-activation retention, actual SQLite persistence, public Store close and process loss require separate actual delivery controls. The proposed read activation's weak retention must start before Store construction can be captured; a late weak SQL tap cannot undo an earlier strong resource capture. Other ancestors' established policies must remain independent. A direct SQL fact must concern the exact same-generation object obtained once at the original receiver point and must not guess a DB owner from a type or numeric ID.

No whole-input, all-history, current-cold or whole-native closure is claimed. Product source, existing fixtures and their test budgets are unchanged.
